content:
Ethan Chen: Quick follow-up from today — a few runtime questions that came up during the demo. I can answer live but dropping clarifications here for folks who couldn't make it.
Priya Patel: Is the short-term plan to prioritize batching improvements or kernel-level attention optimizations?
Ethan Chen: Short answer: both, but different tracks. Batching/caching work (team B) is highest-impact for 95p latency now; kernel attention work (team K) targets tail latency and cost later in the quarter.
Sofia Nguyen: Can you clarify what we mean by '95p latency' in the roadmap doc? is that p95 per-token or per-response?
Ethan Chen: p95 for end-to-end responses on our default 512-token workload. We should add that to the public roadmap note.
Diego Ramos: For batching, are we planning more aggressive prompt coalescing or smarter batching windows? any change to the default batch_time_ms?
Ethan Chen: Smarter windows + adaptive coalescing. Default batch_time_ms stays 8ms, but we'll add adaptive mode that increases for bursty tails.
Ava Li: Any compatibility concerns with quantized kernels when we change batching behavior? last time we saw KV cache edge cases.
Priya Patel: Yup we hit a `kv-cache mismatch` in staging with q8 kernels, tracked in ENG-421. Workaround was to fall back to fp16 shards.
Ethan Chen: Plan: kernel team will add validation across quantization paths; control-plane will auto-fallback to compatible variant on detection. Fallback policy: prefer same model variant with different kernel; then different quantization; then different region.
Sofia Nguyen: ETA on fallbacks work? customers worried about silent quality drops.
Ethan Chen: Canary starts next week (team K). Full rollout guarded by canary + traffic ramp with automatic rollback triggers (latency > 2x or quality drift on our eval set).
Diego Ramos: What metrics will trigger rollback? need specifics so we can add alerts in Console.
Ethan Chen: Primary SLIs: p95 response latency, error rate, and eval-set BLEU/ROUGE delta > 3% for regen tests. Ops will add dashboard slices per-route.
Ava Li: Can we get a snippet of the canary config so infra can pre-provision capacity?
Ethan Chen: Sure, example below:
```
canary: true
traffic: 5%
monitoring: [p95_latency, error_rate, eval_delta]
rollback: on_alert
```
Priya Patel: Will the canary use dedicated GPUs or shared hosts? costs?
Ethan Chen: Shared hosts with capacity reservations, team will open a Dedicated request if we need predictable perf. We'll monitor cost impact during canary.
ops-bot: Canary deploy started for `kernel-q8-fallbacks` — canary id c-20260323-17 — 5% traffic -> monitoring enabled.
Sofia Nguyen: Thanks — if we catch any regressions please ping #eng-runtime and tag me.
Ethan Chen: Will do. If anyone has experimental workloads that want to opt into the canary early DM me with model name + route. :thumbsup:
Priya Patel: One last ask — can documentation include a short flow diagram for the fallback order? helps CS and SRE teams.
Ethan Chen: Good call. I'll draft and ping docs. Closing the loop here — will post canary results in this thread.
